newsitem.title: INDIA: India moves to deregulate sugar exports.
newsitem.headline: India moves to deregulate sugar exports.

text.p: India's lower house of parliament on Thursday approved a bill aimed at deregulating sugar exports, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
The new measure will ensure the production of good quality sugar and end the present monopoly of a single trading agency, PTI quoted Indian Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav as telling parliament.
The bill is considered an important step towards freeing the sugar industry from a decades-old system of licensing, pricing and distribution.

India began abolishing licenses for many industries under a reform programme that began in 1991, but it kept sugar under the old regime which has subsidised the price for consumers and protected producers.

Indian sugar exports are currently channelled through the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export-Import Corp (ISGIEC), an agency set up by private millers. It is the only body permitted to export sugar.

The bill seeks to repeal the Sugar Export Promotion Act of 1958. It will permit private entrepreneurs registered with the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Development Association (APEDA) to export sugar. --New Delhi newsroom +91-22-3012024
